memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaites, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salekah, all of Bashan to the border of the people of Geshur and Maakah, and half of Gilead to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon. Moses, the servant of the Lord, and the Israelites conquered them. And Moses the servant of the Lord gave their land to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh to be their possession - Josh 12:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Og of Bashan was no ordinary king. He was one of the last of the Rephaites — the giants — a man whose iron bed was so large it became famous (Deut 3:11). If any enemy looked unbeatable on paper, it was Og. And yet here he is, tucked into a list of the defeated. The giant king fell, and his land was handed over as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.

Notice how the passage keeps calling Moses "the servant of the Lord." The victory is credited not to Moses' brilliance but to the Lord whom he served. Moses conquered, yes — but as a servant, under orders, in God's strength. The giant fell because God gave him into Israel's hand.

We all have our Ogs — the fears and obstacles that seem too big, too entrenched, too powerful to overcome. This list quietly insists that no giant is beyond God's reach. The same Lord who toppled Og still specialises in bringing down what looks unbeatable. And the greatest giants of all — sin and death itself — have already been laid low by Christ, who through His death destroyed the one who held the power of death (Heb 2:14-15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "giant" in your life feels too big to overcome?
- Does it encourage you that even Og ended up on the list of the defeated?
- How does Christ's victory over sin and death shrink your giants down to size?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, the giants I face feel far bigger than me. Thank You that no obstacle is too large for You, and that in Christ even death is already defeated. Amen.
